graph.name: Roche AWS Processing Bubble and Data Hub Architecture
graph.notes: Roche's architecture pattern decouples permanent, compliant storage (Data Hub with S3, Redshift, Lake Formation) from temporary data science compute environments ('Bubbles' with SageMaker, Athena, EKS). Environments are provisioned automatically via ServiceNow, Service Catalog, and CloudFormation, followed by read-only data cross-sharing.

nodes.name: Users
nodes.notes: Data scientists and analysts requesting environment creation and data access.

nodes.name: Service Catalog
nodes.notes: Provides standard, automated environment templates triggered by ticket requests.

nodes.name: CloudFormation
nodes.notes: Automates template-driven deployment of isolated processing environments ('Bubbles').

nodes.name: SageMaker
nodes.notes: Machine learning workspace running inside the isolated processing bubble.

nodes.name: Athena
nodes.notes: Interactive query service provisioned within the processing bubble.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Kubernetes container service deployed in the processing environment for data workloads.

nodes.name: DataHub GUI
nodes.notes: Custom web application GUI for dataset discovery and requesting data access.

nodes.name: RedShift
nodes.notes: Data warehousing service in the persistent Data Hub layer.

nodes.name: Lake Formation
nodes.notes: Automates permissions, metadata management, and cross-account data sharing.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Central object storage for immutable persistent datasets in the Data Hub.

edges.notes: User submits an environment request via ServiceNow which triggers AWS Service Catalog.
Service Catalog invokes CloudFormation template creation steps.
CloudFormation provisions SageMaker into the new isolated bubble environment.
CloudFormation provisions Athena into the new isolated bubble environment.
CloudFormation provisions EKS cluster into the new isolated bubble environment.
User uses DataHub GUI to search the catalog and submit a data access request.
Approved requests trigger Lake Formation to configure cross-account dataset access.
S3 buckets are shared in read-only mode directly to the user's processing bubble.
